back: A family of compounds with the same functional group and general formula; successive members differ by CH₂, have similar chemical properties and a gradual trend in physical properties.
The atom or group of atoms responsible for the characteristic reactions of a compound.
Saturated: only C–C single bonds. Unsaturated: at least one C=C or C≡C multiple bond.
Alkanes CₙH₂ₙ₊₂; alkenes CₙH₂ₙ; alcohols CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH.
Alkyl group from the alcohol first, then the acid part with -oate: CH₃COOCH₂CH₃ is ethyl ethanoate.

front: Which carbons count in -al, -oic acid and -nitrile names?
back: The carbon of –CHO, –COOH and –C≡N is carbon 1 and counts in the stem: CH₃CH₂CN is propanenitrile.
Count the carbons bonded to the C–OH carbon: one (1°), two (2°), three (3°).
Each line end and corner is a carbon; hydrogens on carbon are not shown; every other atom (O, N, halogens) and H on them is written.
The simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element in a compound.
Longest chain containing the functional group; lowest number for the functional group; prefixes alphabetical with locants; di-/tri- for repeats.
